subject: FinNova follow-up: processing locality, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer details
messages:
From: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@finnova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: CloudOps FinNova <cloudops@finnova.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on where data is processed and subprocessors

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team found the latency profiles helpful. Before we proceed to procurement we need to confirm a few things for our security and legal review so we can complete an internal memo:

1) Primary processing locations: where will FinNova request payloads and KV cache be processed by default (region/zone)?
2) Subprocessors: a list of third parties that may touch request content or metadata (including cloud providers, logging, monitoring). For each, where are their processing locations (if applicable)?
3) Cross-border transfers: do you ever route data outside the customer region for serving or observability? If so, under what conditions and safeguards?
4) Retention & deletion: default retention for request payloads, KV cache, logs; how deletion requests are handled and expected timelines (including backups).

We appreciate concise answers; legal is particularly sensitive to backups, and CloudOps wants to know whether inference occurs in our EU region or hops to US endpoints.

Cheers,
Maria
Maria Garcia
Director, Cloud Security
FinNova

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@finnova.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed and subprocessors

Hi Maria — thanks, and good questions. Quick answers up front, then I attached a high-level data-flow diagram and our latest SOC 2 snapshot for your legal team. More detail below.

TL;DR
- Primary processing: Requests are served in the customer-selected region (we support us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, asia-southeast1).
- Subprocessors: AWS (compute + S3), GCP (optional regions), Datadog (monitoring), Cloudflare (CDN), Fastly (optional caching), Segment (optional analytics) — we list region specifics below.
- Cross-border transfers: We do not cross-border route request bodies by default. Fallbacks to compatible regions occur only under capacity outages or approved routing policies, and are logged and encrypt-protected.
- Retention: Default request payload retention 30 days for hosted API traces; KV cache retention configurable by customer (default 7 days); logs/metrics retained per plan (30/90/365 days options). Deletion requests propagate to primary stores within 24 hours; full removal from backups may take up to 90 days.

Details (short):
1) Processing locality: Customers pick the serving region at provisioning. For FinNova we recommend provisioning in eu-west-1 for EU-resident data. Serving nodes and KV caches are created in that region. Model weights may be pulled from a global artifact store but are loaded into local region nodes; weights are not treated as customer data.

2) Subprocessors and where they may process data:
- AWS (EC2/EKS & S3): primary compute and object storage in the selected region (e.g., us-east-1 or eu-west-1).
- GCP (GCE & GCS): available as an alternative region provider; used only if customer selects GCP regions.
- Cloudflare: edge routing and DDoS protection; metadata (IP, geolocation) may be processed at edge locations for routing decisions. Content bodies are not persisted at the edge.
- Fastly: optional accelerator for streaming; only used when configured — edge locations may cache transient chunks for latency improvements.
- Datadog: monitoring metrics and traces (no request bodies) — hosts and anonymized traces may be sent to Datadog in US or EU depending on plan.
- Segment / Analytics vendors: only used when customer opts into analytics; region depends on vendor settings.

3) Cross-border transfer handling:
- Default behavior: No customer request payloads leave the customer-selected region. Traffic ingress is regional and routed to local serving nodes.
- Exceptions: automatic failover to another region can occur when the primary region is degraded. Failover is governed by a policy you control (we propose canary/auto-fail to eu-west-1 only, or manual DR). Any cross-region failover is recorded in audit logs and accompanied by automatic encryption in transit (TLS 1.3) and at rest.
- Observability: metrics and traces are redacted by default; full request bodies are not forwarded to external monitoring. Where we aggregate telemetry that includes low-sensitivity metadata, it is sent to the monitoring endpoint region configured for the account.

4) Retention & deletion:
- Request payloads (hosted API traces): default 30 days; customer can request shorter retention or opt into no retention.
- KV cache (inference cache): default 7 days; configurable and can be turned off for strict residency needs.
- Audit logs: 90 days default; extended retention is an add-on.
- Deletion workflow: a deletion API and portal action will mark data for deletion; primary stores are cleared within 24 hours; garbage collection removes data from snapshots and cold backups within 90 days. We provide a deletion confirmation report once GC completes.

I've attached the data-flow diagram that maps requests to subprocessors. Let us know if you want us to produce a tailored diagram for your eu-west-1-only setup.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-data-flow-diagram.pdf (PDF)]

From: legal@finnova.com <legal@finnova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Maria Garcia <maria.garcia@finnova.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Questions on where data is processed and subprocessors

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. A couple of follow-ups from our privacy counsel:

- Backups: you note up to 90 days for removal from backups. Can you confirm whether backups are encrypted with a customer-specific KMS key (BYOK) or Redwood-managed keys? We need to understand key scoping if backups are stored out-of-region.
- Subprocessor list: can you provide a static list we can reference in the contract (including any sub-subprocessors such as managed service providers)?
- Cross-border logging: if failover occurs and we have EU-only routing policy, will you produce a real-time notification with time and target region? We also want a timeline for when the data will be moved back to EU once primary region heals.

Please reply and copy compliance@finnova if you need to raise any contractual exceptions.

Thanks,
FinNova Legal

Hi — responding inline to legal and adding specifics. Copying Dev and Marcus for the implementation notes.

1) Backups & KMS
- We support both Redwood-managed keys and BYOK (customer-managed KMS). For FinNova we recommend BYOK scoped to the eu-west-1 key if you require region-scoped key material. Backups are encrypted at rest with the same KMS; when BYOK is enabled, backup encryption keys are under your control (we will hold key access only for operations if explicitly granted).
- Backups may be replicated for DR only when you enable cross-region DR; otherwise they remain in-region. Cross-region backup replication is off by default.

2) Static subprocessor list (core services that may process or handle metadata):
- Amazon Web Services (EC2, EKS, S3) — regional (us/eu/apac)
- Google Cloud Platform (GCE, GCS) — regional, on-request
- Cloudflare (edge routing & WAF) — edge locations globally for routing metadata
- Fastly (optional streaming/cache) — edge cache nodes when enabled
- Datadog (metrics & traces) — US/EU endpoints depending on tenancy
- Sumo Logic / Logging partners (where enabled) — region depends on account config
- HashiCorp Vault (secrets management, where enabled) — hosted or self-managed options
- PagerDuty / Opsgenie (alerting) — metadata only

We maintain a complete subprocessor register (including sub-subprocessors) and can provide that as an appendix for contract exhibit. We also publish the list and region coverage in our security portal (link below).

3) Cross-border failover notifications & restoration
- Notification: We will send a real-time incident notification to the configured on-call and compliance@finnova when automatic failover moves traffic to an alternative region. The notification includes timestamps, source region, target region, and estimated duration.
- Restoration timeline: Once the primary region is healthy, traffic can be routed back automatically or manually per your policy. Automatic rehydration of caches back to the primary region is attempted within 24–72 hours; persistent customer data (e.g., KV entries created during failover) are replicated back when safe and governed by your retention/consistency setting.

Next steps:
- If you want BYOK for eu-west-1 backups, let us know and our ops team will provision a tenancy plan and a short onboarding checklist.
- I will attach our subprocessor register (redacted for public view) and provide the full appendix under NDA if needed.
